name: Monaco Blue
why: A notably complete off-grid 450F at the core budget ceiling: 2024 standing rigging, 1,200Ah LiFePO4 house bank, 1,800W solar, Victron Quattro 3kW inverter/charger, 2023 40 GPH watermaker, inverter-capable aft-cabin A/C, low-hour MASE generator and 2025 barrier coat/antifouling. The current owners have cruised the Mediterranean, crossed the Atlantic and spent the last year-plus in the Caribbean/Bahamas, so the boat has a much more proven liveaboard profile than a fresh fleet-exit candidate.
risks: 2012 hull with Yanmar engine hours represented around 3,800 on the current broker page; exact saildrive service and major-engine-service history still need documentation. The current owners originally bought the boat from a small Croatian charter company. There is no current seller survey/moisture report, routine service has often been owner-performed, and major-system invoices are still being gathered. Broker says the bulkheads were addressed in the Mediterranean and has provided a photo folder, but the scope and documentation need review rather than relying on listing language alone. Native electrical system is 220V.

next_step: Review the broker's bulkhead photo folder and wait for the major-system invoices/service records promised by Bill, focusing on the 2024 rig, bulkhead work, engine/saildrive history, lithium/Victron installation, generator and 2025 bottom work. name: Captiva
why: One-owner-since-new, never-chartered 3-cabin owner's version with a strong comfort inventory: upgraded SD60 saildrives, fresh bottom paint and saildrive seals in Aug. 2026, 2022 mainsail, 11kVA Onan, 42,000 BTU CruisAir, Spectra watermaker, custom solar targa, eight-battery house bank, inverter/isolation transformers, diesel heat, washer/dryer, radar and Starlink. The private-use history and current yard maintenance make it substantially more interesting than a similarly aged charter 440.
risks: 2008 hull and current engine/generator hours are still unknown despite the listing calling engine hours low. Standing-rig replacement age is not disclosed. The 2021 house bank is eight 12V/220Ah deep-cycle batteries with chemistry not identified as lithium, solar wattage is not published and the inverter is only 1,850W, so the electrical system may need meaningful modernization for battery-based A/C. The generator's raw-water lift pump is listed as not installed. Broker says the older owner is not tech savvy and that obtaining electronic records will be nearly impossible, so casualty/structure/moisture history and the maintenance baseline may have to be established through direct answers and survey rather than a clean document archive.
stage: Broker replied — records difficult; basic-facts reply draft queued
next_step: Use the queued email-first reply to get only the decision-driving basics while Captiva is still in the yard: current engine/generator hours, standing-rig age, approximate solar/house-bank setup, material collision/grounding/storm/structural history and remaining post-yard projects. Decide whether a call is worthwhile only after that baseline arrives; no phone number or travel commitment was provided automatically.
